findings.title: Workflow reminder cancellation (and the new `cancelled` DB write the whole fix depends on) is fire-and-forget
findings.body: In the `forEach` loop that replaced the old explicit `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` logic, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` are called without being awaited or collected into the `prismaPromises` array that is later awaited via `Promise.all`. Previously the handler explicitly awaited the DB deletion of each `workflowReminder` row before returning, guaranteeing durability. Now, for EMAIL reminders, the critical write (`cancelled: true`) that the entire PR's fix relies on happens inside an un-awaited async call. If the Next.js API route/serverless function finishes and the response is returned before that promise resolves, the write may never complete, silently defeating the fix and allowing the reminder to still be sent.

findings.title: Reschedule-cancellation of workflow reminders is fire-and-forget, no longer awaited
findings.body: In `requestReschedule`, the previous code collected `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` promises into `remindersToDelete` and awaited them with `Promise.all` before continuing. That collection/await has been removed; now `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` are invoked inside a `forEach` with no awaiting at all. The DB write that marks the reminder as `cancelled` (for EMAIL) is therefore not guaranteed to complete before the trpc mutation resolves and the request lifecycle ends, risking the reminder remaining un-flagged and still being sent by SendGrid.

findings.title: A single failed SendGrid cancel request aborts processing of all remaining pending cancellations for the run
findings.body: The `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop and the subsequent `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` are wrapped in one try/catch. If `client.request` throws for any single reminder (e.g. invalid/null `referenceId`, SendGrid rate limiting, or a batch already cancelled), execution jumps straight to the catch block: every reminder later in the array that hasn't been iterated yet is skipped entirely for that run, and even reminders already successfully cancelled earlier in the loop never get their `workflowReminder.delete` committed because `Promise.all` is never reached. Since this cron is the mechanism the whole PR relies on to actually cancel reminders before they're sent, one bad row can block cancellation of every other pending reminder in that run (and potentially every subsequent run if the same row keeps failing), reintroducing the risk the PR set out to fix.

findings.title: `remindersToCancel` query is missing a `method: EMAIL` filter
findings.body: The query `prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: {...} } })` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` filter, even though this cron endpoint and the subsequent code treat `reminder.referenceId` as a SendGrid batch id. Today this works only because SMS cancellation (`deleteScheduledSMSReminder`) never sets `cancelled: true`. This is an implicit, undocumented invariant across two separate files; if any future code path sets `cancelled: true` on a non-EMAIL reminder, this cron will send a Twilio SID (or other non-SendGrid id) to the SendGrid cancel endpoint as `batch_id`, causing spurious API errors (which, per the loop-abort issue, could also block other cancellations).

findings.title: Reschedule flow still cancels SendGrid email reminders immediately instead of using the new deferred-cancellation strategy
findings.body: For the cancel flow, this PR defers actual SendGrid cancellation to the `scheduleEmailReminders` cron (only cancelling within 1 hour of send time) specifically to avoid hitting SendGrid's ~100 pending-cancellation limit that caused the original bug. However, the reschedule flow calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` with `immediateDelete = true`, which cancels at SendGrid synchronously regardless of how far in the future the original `scheduledDate` is. Since rescheduling can happen for reminders scheduled well in the future (up to 72 hours), a burst of reschedules can still accumulate many pending SendGrid cancellations exactly as before, partially reintroducing the root cause for the "rescheduled bookings" case the PR title explicitly calls out.

findings.title: `immediateDelete` branch leaves a stale `WorkflowReminder` row in the database
findings.body: When `immediateDelete` is true, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` only calls the SendGrid cancel endpoint and returns; it neither deletes the `WorkflowReminder` row nor sets `cancelled: true` on it. For the reschedule path (`handleNewBooking.ts`), the original booking is not deleted, so this row is never cleaned up by cascade; it will sit in the table (with `scheduled: true`, `cancelled` unset) until the unrelated 'delete all EMAIL reminders past their scheduledDate' cleanup in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` eventually removes it — which can take up to 72 hours. This is a data-hygiene gap left over from the refactor.

findings.title: Unused `Prisma` import after removing `Prisma.BatchPayload`-typed deletion arrays
findings.body: `Prisma` is imported from `@prisma/client` (line 9) but the only place it was previously used — `PrismaPromise<Prisma.BatchPayload>[]` arrays for `remindersToDelete`/`deleteReminderPromise` — has been removed as part of this refactor. No other usage of the `Prisma` namespace remains in the file, so this import is now dead code, which will trigger `no-unused-vars`/unused-import lint errors in a codebase that appears to enforce strict linting, and should be removed.

findings.title: No tests added for the new cancellation flow or the `cancelled` flag semantics
findings.body: This PR introduces a new `cancelled` field, changes the signatures of `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder`, and adds a new cancellation branch to the `scheduleEmailReminders` cron that is the core mechanism fixing the reported bug (reminders still sent after cancel/reschedule). No unit or integration tests are included to verify that: cancelling/rescheduling a booking marks the reminder `cancelled`; the cron correctly cancels and removes reminders whose scheduledDate falls within the next hour; or that a failure for one reminder doesn't silently drop others. Given this is explicitly a bug-fix PR for a subtle, hard-to-notice regression (emails silently still sending), the lack of regression tests is a significant gap.
